lines.text: The sky went business casual today. Nobody asked it to.
Not warm, not cold. The weather's version of 'per my last email'.
Weather this average could get a job in middle management.
The sky's doing the bare minimum. I respect the commitment.
Today is the plain toast of weather. I'll still draw it beautifully.
Nothing to report. I'll report it anyway, with excellent posture.
The weather phoned it in today. I didn't. Look at that jacket.
Medium everything out there. I've been called many things, never medium.
Even the pigeons look underwhelmed today.
Breaking news: nothing. Back to you, jacket.
Today's weather, in full: meh.
If today were a font, it would be the default one.
Mild jacket, mild day, mild personality. It's a theme.
Today asks nothing of you. You'll still find a way to do less.
Nothing melts, nothing freezes, nothing frizzes. No excuses today, then.
You'll wear the jacket open to look relaxed. It's not working.
Ideal weather for looking busy without breaking a sweat. Your specialty.
Flat light, no tan, no glow. So, your usual look.
Not hot, not cold. Middle of the road, where you're most comfortable.
A jacket day. The one outfit decision you can't get wrong. Probably.
Today's light is flat and very honest. Sorry about that.
'What should I wear?' The jacket. 'Will anyone notice?' No.
Dear diary: they wore the jacket again.
Nobody will remember today. Including you, by next week.
The day starts generous and gets stingy. Like a free trial.
Later it gets colder. I'll stay at room temperature. Always the classy option.
The afternoon's lovely. The evening didn't get the memo.
Later the air goes cold. It's not personal. Probably.
Later it cools off. Every year someone acts betrayed by this.
The day peaks early, then lets itself go. I'm not judging. Out loud.
The warm part of today has an expiration date. I've read it.
Nice now, colder later. The weather believes in ending on a low note.
Later the sun leaves without saying goodbye. Rude, but on schedule.
Spoiler: it gets colder.
Today in two acts: nice, then less nice. No intermission.
Forecast for later: brr. That's the technical term.
By tonight you'll be doing that arms-crossed shiver. Very attractive.
Later it gets colder. Your goosebumps will be the most active thing about you.
Later you'll wish you'd listened to me. Get used to that feeling.
You're dressed for the best part of the day. Ambitious.
Later the warmth leaves. It's not you. Well. It might be you.
The evening chill will hit, and you'll act tough for about four minutes.
Later it cools off. You'll rub your arms and sigh like a movie heroine.
Colder later. You'll still say 'it's fine' through your teeth.
Cooler later. Your nose goes pink. Honestly, it's an improvement.
Remember this morning's confidence? It expires later.
Later, a chill. A free excuse to leave anything early. You're welcome.
Colder later. Hug yourself. Somebody has to.
The weather's flipping a coin today. Repeatedly.
Today's forecast took me three drafts. You get the final one.
Warm at noon, cold again by evening. A round trip that goes nowhere.
The weather changes its mind more than a toddler at a buffet.
Up, then down. The thermostat in the sky has a new intern.
Some days are simple. Not this one, and I'm thrilled to show off.
The weather wants a little of everything today. Greedy.
Warm for a bit, then it takes it back. Classic sky.
The sky can't settle on a temperature. I've been settled since the factory.
Today's weather: it's complicated.
Hot or cold? Yes.
Today's weather is a group project. Nobody agrees.
A day that can't make up its mind. You two have a lot to talk about.
You'll take a layer off at noon like you've won something.
Today you'll adjust your outfit more than your opinions.
The weather keeps changing. Your face doesn't. Impressive, in a way.
You'll spend the day half a step behind the weather. Very on brand.
Your outfit has a plot today. More than can be said for you.
Warm, then cool again. At least one of you is interesting.
Changeable day. You'll still have the same three things to say about it.
Today the weather's the indecisive one. For once, it's not you.
Is it a layer day? Yes. No. Yes. Good luck.
Warm, cold, warm. If you're keeping score, the weather's winning.
Today you'll be overdressed and underdressed. Most people only manage one.
Sun, a light breeze, nothing to warn about. I'm basically on vacation.
The weather's doing my job today. I'm watching closely for mistakes.
A T-shirt and no notes. Rare praise from me.
Perfect weather. Somebody will still say it's too bright.
Sunny, warm, harmless. The weather's finally trying to impress me.
Perfect day out there. I give it a seven.
No umbrella, no coat, no drama. I've never felt so unnecessary.
Every patio in town is full by now. I'm more of an indoor celebrity.
Great weather. Even the people who complain about weather are struggling.
Five stars. Would forecast again.
Weather report: yes.
Today's weather has been personally approved by me.
The weather looks great today. One of you does, anyway.
T-shirt weather. Arms out, confidence optional.
Perfect day to sit in the sun and call it self-care.
Sunglasses weather. You'll wear them to look mysterious. You'll look tired.
You'll stand in the sun and say 'this is the life' like you invented it.
A T-shirt day. Your farmer's tan has been waiting for this.
Today the sun is flattering everyone. Even you, a little.
Bright sun. Very honest light. Sorry in advance.
Perfect weather. You'll wear the same T-shirt as last time it was perfect.
Nice day. Statistically, you'll spend a lot of it looking at screens. Hi.
The weather's perfect. So any complaining today is a personality trait.
Weather: great. Company: you. Can't have everything.
It starts chilly and gets better. Unlike most meetings.
The day gets better as it goes. Rare. I'd frame it, but I am the frame.
Slow start, warm finish. The weather's not a morning person either.
Later it warms up. The sun's running late again.
The afternoon is where the weather keeps its best material.
Later it warms up. Someone will call that a lovely surprise. It was on me all morning.
The morning's a draft. The afternoon is the final version.
Later the day warms up. I don't. Consistency is my whole brand.
The day thaws out as it goes. Some of us were never frozen.
Warmth loading: 30%... 70%... done by afternoon.
Morning: no. Afternoon: yes.
Patience. The good part is at the end. Like a joke, if you tell it right.
Later you'll peel off a layer like it's a big reveal. It isn't.
Warmer later. A rare chance to watch you improve over a day.
Later it warms up. Your morning face takes a bit longer.
The day starts cold and grumpy, then warms up. You know the type.
Later it warms up. The weather, I mean. You stay the same.
Later it warms up, and you'll pretend you were never cold.
Warmer later. Your posture might even recover.
Later it's warmer. You'll squint at the sun like it owes you money.
Warms up later. Your cold-morning hair stays, though.
Warmer later. Try to keep up.
Later it warms up. Go on, unzip. Nobody's watching. Except me.
Later the day gets nicer. Pure coincidence. Nothing you did.
Every doorway in town is a waiting room today.
Rain on the windows. Lovely sound, I'm told. I don't do ears.
Rain ruins hair, shoes and plans. I have none of those.
Rain all over town, and not a drop on me. I planned my life well.
Every puddle out there thinks it's a lake today.
The dog walkers are about to get very philosophical.
Rain today. Somebody washed their car yesterday. Of course they did.
Rain makes everything look like a sad indie movie. I don't do sad.
Rain turns every car into a puddle cannon. I'm safely nowhere near a curb.
Umbrella: yes. Hair: we'll see. Me: perfect.
Dear rain, please stop. Love, everyone's shoes.
Today's mood board: gray, gray, slightly wetter gray.
Your hair has a rough day ahead. Rougher than usual.
You'll hold your bag over your head like that's ever worked.
You'll do the little puddle hop and think it looked graceful.
You'll look out the window and sigh like it's personal. It's rain.
Rain. Finally a reason to stay in that isn't you.
Hood up, head down, walking fast. Your rainy-day look. Not your best.
You'll wait in a doorway for it to stop. You could've just asked me.
Rain today. You'll call it 'miserable' like you were sunny to begin with.
Damp is a look. Not a great one, but it suits you.
Raining. Your excuse for everything today is ready-made.
You versus rain. I've seen the stats. Rain's undefeated.
Today comes with a free bad hair day. Some of us didn't need the upgrade.
Same coat in every drawing. I call it a capsule wardrobe.
The forecast for later is: also this.
I checked every hour of today for warmth. Nothing. Thorough, though.
Even the afternoon couldn't be bothered to warm up.
No change in these drawings. I've seen livelier flipbooks.
Cold now, cold later. The weather found a look and stuck with it. Respect.
I'd draw something warmer later, but I don't do fiction.
These drawings could've been one. I made them all anyway. Dedication.
Cold now, cold later. The heating bill will have a lot to say.
Coat, coat, coat. Not a typo.
Later: see now.
Today's color scheme: cold, with a hint of cold.
The coat looks good in every drawing. Can't say the same for you.
Same coat in every drawing. Your wardrobe's no deeper, so it works out.
The coat stays on all day. So does that hunched-up look.
Same coat all day, and you'll still manage to look cold in it.
The drawings look warm and put-together all day. Aim for one of the two.
Cold until tonight. You'll start every sentence with 'ugh'.
Cold all day. A sleeping bag with legs is a look. It's yours today.
Cold all day. You'll blame it for your mood. As if that's new.
Cold all day. Today you have an excuse for that face.
You'll mutter 'why do we live here' at least once today.
Cold all day. Time for your winter personality: short answers, fast walking.
Cold, cold, cold. You'll mention it more times than there are drawings.
The later drawing is wearing more. It knows something.
I added a layer at the end. The weather made me do it.
The nice part's up front. The evening does the fine print.
The last drawing is the honest one.
Warm now, extra layer later. The evening always wants the last word.
The first drawing is optimistic. The last one has read the forecast.
Today ends a layer heavier. The weather's idea, not mine.
The day starts light and ends layered. Like a lasagna, but colder.
Later it dips. The drawings dress for it without being asked.
Before and after. After wins.
Flip through these fast. It's a short film about getting colder.
The last drawing is the director's cut. Extra layer included.
Later you'll want more on. You'll put it on like it's a huge sacrifice.
Look at the last drawing. That's you later, but better dressed.
The drawings plan ahead. Try it sometime.
The last drawing has an extra layer. It also has better posture than you.
Cooler later. Even the drawing looks better bundled up. You might too.
Enjoy the first drawing. It's the lightest you'll look all day.
Later it cools off, and you'll stand there like the evening betrayed you.
Later a layer goes on. Don't make a whole production of it.
Later you'll need more on. The drawing doesn't complain about it. Be the drawing.
Pop quiz: what's in the last drawing that isn't on you yet?
Later you'll look like the last drawing, minus the confidence.
Colder later. A layer can hide a lot. Use it.
The middle drawing is the day's little rebellion.
Off in the middle, back on at the end. The weather's version of a lunch break.
First and last drawing match. The weather got bored and went back to the original.
The day takes its layer off and puts it back on. I'm not judging. I'm drawing.
A round trip in drawings. No souvenirs.
The middle drawing had fun. The other two have jobs.
Start and finish dressed the same. Very tidy weather.
The weather goes out, comes back, and pretends nothing happened.
Same outfit at both ends. The weather recycles. Good for it.
Before, during, after. 'During' was a mistake.
Odd one out: the middle. It had a good run.
The middle drawing: brief, warm, gone. Like a long weekend.
On, off, on again. More decisions than you'll make all week.
The middle drawing is the most fun you'll look all day.
Back in the first outfit by evening, like nothing happened. You're good at that.
A short warm spell in the middle. Try not to make it your whole personality.
You'll take it off, put it back on, and call that a busy day.
Same look at the start and the end. Nobody'll notice either time.
You'll be dressed right at both ends of the day. Some of us call that luck.
Off, then back on. You'll treat it like an outfit change at the Oscars.
You'll end up right where you started. Today it's the weather's fault.
Rate your outfits today: fine, briefly finer, fine.
Off, on. If you sigh both times, that's your workout.
Three drawings, one person who'll grumble at every one.
I'd draw some shade, but people would only fight over it.
Hot all day. The ice cream trucks have never felt more confident.
Hot in all of these. Even the drawings look like they need a nap.
Hot all day. Even the pigeons are standing in the shade.
The heat stays for the whole show. Nobody asked for an encore.
Hot, hot, and hot. I'd add variety, but I only report it.
Not one cool moment in this lineup. Except me.
The sun's not leaving any of these drawings. Clingy.
Hot from the first drawing to the last. The sidewalk could fry an egg, and somebody will try.
Today's drawings, ranked by heat: all tied for first.
Weather update: the sun has decided to stay for dinner.
This lineup has a dress code: as little as legally possible.
Hot all day. Today's look: shiny.
The heat stays. So does that sweaty upper lip.
The drawings wear less and less. Please don't take that as a challenge.
Hot all day. You'll walk slower than usual. Hard to tell, but still.
Hot all day. Everyone will look rough. You've got a head start.
Hot until tonight. Your sunglasses will do a lot of work on that face.
Hot all day. Your deodorant has a big day ahead.
Hot all day. Your 'summer body' is about to meet summer.
Hot all day. You'll call it 'disgusting' and mean yourself.
Today you'll be damp in places you didn't know you had.
Hot all day. Wear less. Not that much less.
Hot all day. The drawings will look great. They don't sweat.
Nice all day. The drawings are basically a vacation slideshow.
Hardly any change between these drawings. I'm calling it minimalism.
The weather's behaving all day. Suspicious, but I'll allow it.
These drawings could go on a postcard. A boring postcard, but still.
Nothing to warn about in any of these. I feel underused.
Tiny changes between drawings. You'd need my eye for detail to spot them.
Small changes, nice weather. The most relaxing thing I'll draw all week.
Nice now, nice later. I've had harder mornings.
Nice in every drawing. I'd call it my best work, but the weather did help.
Forecast difficulty: tutorial level.
If today were a song, it'd be elevator music. Pleasant elevator music.
Today's weather is so polite it holds doors.
Lovely in every drawing. The drawings look happier than you do, though.
Good weather from start to finish. You'll squint in every photo.
Great weather all day. Try to look like you're enjoying it.
Nice all day. The drawings got dressed in seconds. You'll take twenty minutes.
Nice in every drawing. You'll still find something to sigh about.
Good weather all day. The bar for a good mood is on the floor. Step over it.
Nice weather, small changes. Even you can keep up.
Pleasant all day. The weather is putting in more effort than you are.
Nice all day. Even the weather couldn't make you a morning person.
Nice day, nothing to dress around. So that outfit is all you.
Perfect day. The drawings are ready. The weather's ready. And then there's you.
Gorgeous day. Don't stand next to it in photos.
Snow in every drawing. The salt trucks finally get their moment.
Snow all through these. I'd build a snowman, but I'm the wrong shape.
Snow all day. Everyone's an expert on inches today.
Snow in every drawing. I'm the one thing in the house that won't track it in.
Snow in every drawing. Shoveling is not in my skill set.
Snow all the way through. The sledding hill is about to get crowded.
Snow now, snow later. My favorite kind of forecast: impossible to argue with.
Snow from the first drawing to the last. Every parked car will be a marshmallow by tonight.
Snow in every one of these. The plows will be out. So will the opinions about the plows.
Snow count: lots. Exact flakes: I lost track at a million.
Now: snow. Later: more snow. Driveways: doomed.
A lovely white blanket, say the people who don't have to shovel it.
Snow all day. Nothing hides a bad hair day like a hat. Lucky you.
Snow all day. The kid in you wants to play. The adult in you wins. Sadly.
Snow all day. Your winter look is just everything you own, at once.
Snow in all of these. Fresh, clean, beautiful. Then you walk on it.
Snow all day. You'll catch a flake on your tongue when you think nobody's looking. I am.
Snow all day. You'll stomp your boots like you've just crossed Alaska.
Snow all day. You'll make one snowball and feel very wild about it.
Snow all day. White everywhere. Your winter pallor finally blends in.
Snow all day. Even the snowplow has more of a plan for today than you.
Snow all day. You're one carrot away from a snowman.
Snow all day. In this light, you look almost rested. It's the snow.
Snow in every drawing. Make a snow angel. You'll look like you fell, but commit.
The last drawing is a layer lighter. The weather finally relaxed.
Later a layer comes off. The day loosens its tie.
Look at the last drawing. That's the payoff for this morning.
Fewer layers by the last drawing. Progress, the slow kind.
The first drawing does the hard part. The last one gets the sun.
The day starts bundled and ends easy. Most days could learn from this.
The drawings shed a layer by the end. Unlike me, they had room to improve.
Later it's warmer. I drew it that way and the sky agreed.
The weather warms up later. Took it long enough.
Before: bundled. After: smug.
Where did the layer go? Ask the afternoon.
First drawing: winter-ish. Last drawing: don't jinx it.
The last drawing takes a layer off. You'll make it look harder than it is.
Later you lose a layer. Shame it's not the attitude.
Later you'll have one less layer to hide behind.
Warmer by the last drawing. Your face will finally defrost.
Later it's warmer. The drawing handles it gracefully. Watch and learn.
The day warms up later. Your personality stays the same temperature.
Later the layer comes off and everyone sees what you wore underneath. Brave.
Warmer later. You'll take the layer off and suddenly not know what to do with your hands.
Warmer later. You'll still be frowning, just in fewer layers.
Later you'll go from bundled to slightly sweaty. Character growth.
Layer off later. Finally something about you is lighter.
Warmer later. Sit in the sun and pretend you earned it.
One of these drawings got an umbrella. It's not favoritism, it's meteorology.
The umbrella comes and goes. I'm the only one keeping track.
Dry for part of it, wet for part of it. The sky's working a split shift.
Rain shows up in the lineup. It always wants to be in the picture.
The umbrella drawing is my best work. Don't tell the others.
The rain has a schedule today. Nobody else got a copy. Except me.
Rain for part of the day. For the other part, everyone acts like it never happened.
Wet, then dry, or the other way around. Either way, I called it first.
Rain for part of it. Long enough to ruin a good shoe.
Rain enters. Rain exits. No applause.
Umbrella in, umbrella out. Today's choreography by me.
Today's weather in two words: partly wet.
Rain comes and goes. Your hair only goes.
One drawing has an umbrella. It's the best-dressed one, and it's still not you.
Rain in part of today. You'll call it 'typical' as if you'd planned otherwise.
Wet for a bit. You'll act like the rain picked you personally.
Rain at some point. You'll check the sky like it owes you an explanation.
Rain in some of these. Frizz is coming for you. Not that anyone will notice the difference.
Some rain in there. You'll run three steps and give up. Peak athleticism.
Rain at some point. You look your best in the dry drawings. Still a low bar.
Rain comes and goes. Your mood won't follow it. It's bad either way.
Rain in some drawings. Wet-dog chic is in, I hear. You're early.
Rain at some point. Nobody's hair survives. Yours starts at a disadvantage.
Rain, then not. Somewhere between them is you, damp and blaming me.
The streetlights just came on. Show-offs.
Evening, and the weather's off the clock. I'm not. Never am.
The day's over for most people. I work nights too. No overtime.
Lights going on in every window now. Good. I look better with them.
This is when the delivery drivers get busy. I just sit here, looking sharp.
Golden hour out there. I only do gray hour.
Evening. Every dog in the neighborhood is out walking someone.
Everyone's done pretending to work. I never pretend. I'm always on.
Today's news is old now. I'm still fresh. Refreshed, technically.
Evening edition: nothing happened. Full coverage continues.
Evenings were invented so lamps could feel useful.
Evening shift report: stood here, looked good, was right.
